title: Continuous Load Scan for PRs with Rolling Baseline Anchors
creator: Jordan Kim
description: Objective: Add a lightweight, CI-friendly load scan that runs for each PR and compares observed tokens/sec and p95 latency against a set of rolling baseline anchors to detect meaningful regressions without excessive false positives. Background: Existing CI baselining runs are heavy and often flagged by unrelated noise. We need a lower-latency harness that provides fast feedback inside PRs, is cheap enough to run on every PR for core services, and robust to small environmental variability. Approach: (1) Maintain a small set of rolling baseline anchors (N=3) representing recent golden commits. (2) For each PR, run a short suite of representative requests (configurable scenarios) with controlled input shapes and fixed RNG seeds where applicable to reduce variance. (3) Measure tokens/sec (steady-state token emission rate) and p95 latency of end-to-end inference. (4) Use a robust statistical test (bootstrap + trimmed-mean effect size) to compare the PR sample to the baseline anchor distribution and compute a paired confidence interval for regression magnitude. (5) Gate the PR if the median regression across anchors exceeds a configurable threshold (default: 8% tokens/sec drop or 10% p95 increase) with >= 95% confidence. Lightweightness: Each run should complete under 6 minutes on a small GPU or CPU emulation profile for quick feedback. Artifacts: results.json artifact with raw samples, test metadata, CI runner environment, and a short narrative summary uploaded to S3 and linked in the PR. Integration: Post a summarized GitHub Check with pass/fail + link to a dashboard that shows historical anchors, recent PR history, and a small chart of p95 vs tokens/sec. Fallbacks: When CI environment is noisy or skewed (detected via high sample variance), mark the run as "unstable" rather than failing the PR and surface the recommendation to rerun in a dedicated baseline job.
acceptance_criteria: PR check runs on each PR and completes within target runtime (<= 6 minutes) under CI resource profile
Artifacts (results.json) uploaded and retrievable from S3/GCS with test metadata and raw samples
Statistical comparison computed and posted as GitHub Check with clear pass/fail rationale
False positive rate empirically under 3% when evaluated against historical commits and synthetic noise
Config knobs exposed: anchor count, detection thresholds, scenario selection, and instability policy
Docs updated with runbook describing how to interpret unstable runs and how to add new scenarios
implementation_notes: Runner: build a Docker-based microbench container that can be invoked from GitHub Actions or our internal CI executor
Scenarios: start with 4 lightweight scenarios picking varied sequence lengths (32, 128, 512) and model families (decoder-only, encoder-decoder if applicable)
Measurement: capture token timestamps to compute steady-state tokens/sec; use request-level timings for p95 (compute via sample quantile with interpolation)
Baseline anchors: store the three most recent successful main branch commits with their result artifacts; update anchors weekly via scheduled job
Statistical method: bootstrap each anchor->PR sample pair 2000 iterations, compute median relative change; apply Benjamini-Hochberg style adjustment for multiple scenarios
CI integration: GitHub Checks API to display summary, link results.json and dashboard; for failures, auto-comment template with remediation steps
Storage: results.json schema should include: runner_env, commit_sha, scenario_id, samples_tokens_per_sec, samples_p95_ms, seed, docker_image, runner_logs_url
Cost control: disable full GPU run for small PRs by default — allow opt-in for expanded hardware matrix via label 'perf/slow-path'
risks_and_mitigation: Flaky environments causing false positives -> mitigation: detect high variance and mark 'unstable' + scheduled nightly baseline refresh
Long CI runtime increasing queue time -> mitigation: limit to short scenarios, use cheap CPU profiles with validated correlation to GPU numbers
Anchors staleness (drift) -> mitigation: weekly anchor rotation and manual override endpoint for rollback
Overly strict thresholds blocking flow -> mitigation: start with conservative thresholds and run an observational window (2 weeks) before enforcing hard gates

M2: Multi-scenario rollup logic and artifact upload + basic GitHub Check (2025-02-24)
